title: Adaptive window aggregator for tenant KPI smoothing and latency-derivative metrics
creator: Aisha Rahman
description:
Background: Our current metric ingestion produces per-request kpis (inference_latency_ms, token_cost, model_variant) at high cardinality. Spiky tenants and bursty workloads cause noisy histograms and frequent false positives in regression alerts. We need an aggregation layer that smooths tenant-level time series without masking real regressions, and a new derived metric (latency-derivative) that surfaces rapid tail deterioration faster than static p99 checks.

Goal: Build an adaptive-window aggregator that produces tenant-scoped, low-cardinality KPI rollups (rolling p50/p95/p99, request_rate, latency_derivative) from OTLP and Prometheus upstreams. Implement dual-write migration, dashboarding, and alerting for latency-derivative. Preserve trace linking for sampling and enable causal attribution to model variant and routing decisions.

Scope: prototype sidecar aggregator + ingestion pipeline changes + proto schema v2 for inference_kpi rollup + dashboards and alerts. Exclude long-term storage changes and billing model updates (addressed in follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: A produced inference_kpi_rollup metric for each tenant containing rolling p50/p95/p99, request_rate, and latency_derivative
Dual-write mode: aggregator emits rollups while preserving original per-request metrics; no customer-visible breakage during migration
Latency-derivative dashboard panels added showing per-tenant spikes and correlated traces
Canary rollout to 5% of tenants with automated health checks for ingestion cost and metric fidelity
Alert: latency-derivative threshold triggers page when derivative exceeds configured threshold and sustained for 3 consecutive windows
Documentation: Confluence runbook for aggregator behavior, config knobs, and rollback steps
No more than 5% increase in telemetry ingestion cost at canary stage (measured by token count and bytes)
Retention of trace linking: every rollup record contains a list of exemplar trace_ids for top offenders (bounded to 3 per window)
technical_notes: Aggregator algorithm: adaptive window size based on exponential smoothing of request_rate with floor=1s, ceiling=60s. Window length w = clamp(alpha * recent_rate^{-0.5}, 1s, 60s) to trade latency vs smoothing.
Latency-derivative: compute d = (p99_t - p99_{t-1}) / max(p50_{t-1}, 1ms) to surface relative tail degradation. Emit both absolute and normalized derivative fields.

Proto: add inference_kpi_rollup v2 proto with fields: tenant_id, window_ms, samples_count, p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, latency_derivative_norm, request_rate_rps, exemplar_trace_ids (repeated, capped at 3). Backwards-compatible via new type_url and optional fields.
Cardinality control: rollups must drop high-card labels (request_id, session_id). Keep model_family, model_variant, route_id. Apply canonicalization service for route and model labels before rollup.
Sampling & exemplars: deterministic exemplar selection for top latency samples using reservoir sampling seeded by tenant_id to ensure repeatability across runs.
OTLP/Prom wire: aggregator accepts OTLP metrics and Prometheus scrape inputs; translates into rollup proto and forwards to the telemetry gateway with original metrics in dual-write mode.
Trace linking: aggregator retains up to 3 exemplar trace_ids per window and includes them in rollup proto for UI drilldowns. Ensure privacy-safe handling by hashing trace ids in logs when needed.
Backpressure: implement soft-queue with token-bucket admission at aggregator. If queue saturates, switch to emit coarse-grain tenant counters only and mark rollup as degraded.
Testing: unit tests for windowing math, integration tests with otelcol receiver, load test that simulates 10k TPS across 200 tenants, and e2e validation against dashboard queries.
Migration: dual-write -> compare rollup-derived p99 against sampled per-request p99; define allowed drift threshold (<=5% p99 difference) before increasing rollout percentage.
steps: 1) Design review and proto RFC (w/ security/priv) - owner: Marco - target complete 2026-02-05
2) Implement sidecar aggregator MVP that accepts OTLP metrics and emits inference_kpi_rollup - target 2026-02-12
3) Integrate exemplar trace extraction and deterministic sampling - target 2026-02-14
4) Deploy dual-write canary to staging and 5% production tenants - target 2026-02-18
5) Validate metric fidelity with automated check and dashboard comparisons - target 2026-02-20
6) Iterate on thresholds and backpressure behavior, then ramp to 50% if stable - target 2026-02-24
7) Full rollout and deprecate dual-write within 2 weeks after stable ramp
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: increased ingestion cost from dual-write - Mitigation: built-in cost guardrails and strict canary budget; abort if >5% predicted increase
Risk: label explosion due to uncanonicalized route/model labels - Mitigation: use label canonicalizer and drop unknowns in aggregator
Risk: missed regressions if smoothing window too large - Mitigation: adaptive window that shortens on sudden rate drops and derivative metric to catch fast changes
Risk: exemplar trace leakage/privacy - Mitigation: limit exemplar count, redact sensitive attributes, and optionally hash trace_ids in audit logs
